newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bank Umum up sharply on acquisition talk.
newsitem.headline: Bank Umum up sharply on acquisition talk.

text.p: Shares of privately-owned PT Bank Umum Nasional rose sharply on Wednesday on market talk it would acquire a stake in PT Bank Perniagaan, brokers said.
One local broker said there was a rumour that the central bank had appointed Bank Umum to assist Bank Perniagaan, which was rumoured to be facing liquidity problems.
Bank Umum shares price rose 20.27 percent to 2,225 rupiah in late morning before ending the first session at 2,200 rupiah on a volume of 1.2 million shares.
A Bank Umum Nasional official declined to comment on the rumours, saying there had been no official appointment of Bank Umum by the central bank to rescue Bank Perniagaan.
"What I know is we had some discussions with the central bank that BUN (Bank Umum) will help in the management of Bank Perniagaan," she said, declining to give further details.
Bank Umum, 40.08-percent owned by business tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, was previously rumoured to be interested in helping privately-owned PT Bank Pacific solve its financial problems.
Hasan is president-commissioner of both Bank Umum and Astra International, Indonesia's top carmaker.

Brokers said market speculation of possible mergers or acquisitions among banks was sparked by repeated calls by the Central Bank Governor for small banks to merge in order to improve efficieny in the industry.
